subject.title: [Bug]: browser in docker hidden in cache folder

question: Should OpenClaw Docker browser-enabled images keep the current `/home/node/.cache/ms-playwright` cache with runtime autodetection, or migrate browser assets to an `/opt` path and expose stable `chrome` and `chromium` commands?
rationale: Current source, docs, release validation, and tests preserve the home-cache contract, while prior `/opt` attempts were closed or conflicting and the remaining change would alter Docker defaults and upgrade behavior.

options.title: Keep Current Cache Contract
options.body: Treat merged Playwright autodetection as the fix for brittle versioned paths and leave `/opt` plus PATH aliases out unless stronger migration evidence appears.

options.title: Approve `/opt` Plus PATH Migration
options.body: Require a focused Dockerfile/docs/test change with live proof for browser-enabled, browser-disabled, runtime-install, mounted-cache, and upgrade scenarios.

options.title: Narrow To PATH Aliases
options.body: Keep the current cache location but add layout-aware `chrome` and `chromium` aliases only if maintainers want that Docker command surface.

recommendation.title: Keep Current Cache Contract
recommendation.body: Treat merged Playwright autodetection as the fix for brittle versioned paths and leave `/opt` plus PATH aliases out unless stronger migration evidence appears.

likelyOwner.reason: Their close comment on the prior same-repository `/opt/playwright` PR is the clearest maintainer-direction signal found for this Docker image contract.
